# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Working draft — English edition in progress (November 27, 2026)
This book is the LEEDUCA group's workspace for the technical manual of the platform. Its content is under review and may change. Please do not cite it yet as a final version. The **[Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/)** is the reference and is more complete; this English edition is being built chapter by chapter, starting with what reviewers of our articles and international colleagues need.
:::

The LEEDUCA/PRELEO platform assesses children aged 3 to 11 in schools in Málaga (Spain) online, three times per school year (3-year-olds since 2023/24). It covers letter knowledge, phonological awareness, rapid automatized naming, word and text reading, reading comprehension, oral language, mathematics and executive functions. Since 2014 it has gathered data from several birth cohorts, named by their year of birth (2010, 2011, 2012…).

The manual describes every task on the platform with the same structure: what it measures and how it is administered, the sample it has been studied in, its reliability and validity, how its scores are interpreted (norms), and which variables affect them. It is written for three kinds of readers:

- **Teachers and school psychologists**, who use the platform's reports and need to know how far a score can be trusted.
- **Clinicians**, who compare LEEDUCA with other tests and need well-justified norms and cut-off scores.
- **Researchers and reviewers**, who want to check every figure.

## Origins

The platform and this manual grew out of the **DIS-ESP battery**, created by María Soledad Carrillo (University of Murcia, a member of the group) and Jesús Alegría (Université Libre de Bruxelles). DIS-ESP proposed a two-stage assessment of dyslexia: group screening of reading efficiency with TECLE and, for the children it flagged, an assessment of the two reading mechanisms, phonological and orthographic [@carrillo2011prevalencia]. The LEEDUCA group promoted it in Málaga on paper (2007–2012) and then moved it to an online platform, which added the early literacy precursors from age 4 and assessment three times per school year.

## How to read this book

Each task sheet has three layers:

1. **The text**, with the results and what they mean.
2. **The full tables**, at the end of each sheet. They are read from the files in `datos/agregados/`, which contain only aggregated results (means, percentiles, correlations…), never data from an individual child.
3. **The code**, in the GitHub repository (button in the sidebar). Tables are computed with R scripts from the complete data, which for privacy reasons never leave the project's computer. The book is built from those tables, so anyone can reproduce its figures.

## Privacy

This book contains only aggregated data. Pupils' names and identification numbers, teachers' names and individual data stay in the project folder at the University of Málaga. Teachers always appear under pseudonyms. Norms of commercial tests used for comparison (PROLEC-R, EDICOLE) are not reproduced, only cited.
